cards.title: A star runs out of fuel
cards.idea: A giant star burns fuel to push outward against its own gravity pulling inward. When fuel ends, gravity wins and the core collapses.

interaction.prompt: Tap the star's core after its fuel runs out.

cards.reveal: The core crushes inward under gravity. A very massive core keeps collapsing into an incredibly tiny, dense point.

cards.title: Escape speed grows with density
cards.idea: To escape any object you need a minimum speed. Squeeze the same mass smaller and the escape speed at its surface climbs higher.

interaction.prompt: Slide to shrink the object's size while keeping its mass fixed.

cards.reveal: As size shrinks, escape speed rises. Shrink far enough and escape speed passes the speed of light. Now even light cannot leave.

cards.title: The point of no return
cards.idea: Around a black hole is an invisible boundary. Cross it and no signal, no light, nothing can come back out.

interaction.prompt: Tap the boundary where light can no longer escape.

cards.reveal: That boundary is the event horizon. Inside it, escape speed exceeds light speed, so the region looks perfectly black.

cards.title: Naming it
cards.idea: A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape from inside its event horizon.

interaction.prompt: Type the name of the boundary you cannot return from.

cards.reveal: Event horizon. It is not a solid surface, just the line marking where escape becomes impossible.

cards.title: Seeing the unseeable
cards.idea: A black hole emits no light, so we cannot see it directly. We spot it by its pull on nearby stars and glowing gas.

interaction.prompt: Tap the swirling gas heating up as it falls in.

cards.reveal: Infalling gas heats and glows brightly before crossing the horizon. That glow and orbiting stars reveal the hidden black hole.

workbook.prompt: Why does a black hole look black?
options: It is made of black material
Not even light can escape from inside it
workbook.answer: Not even light can escape from inside it
